practice_description.medium: Video, installation, immersive environments, digital art, performance, healing practices, VR
practice_description.practice_summary: French Guianese artist working across new media, healing practices, and ancestral knowledge systems to challenge the colonial and extractive frameworks embedded in digital technology. Her work connects internet infrastructure, data colonialism, and algorithmic bias to longer histories of extraction, proposing indigenous and spiritual knowledge as alternative technological paradigms.
practice_description.methodology: Rezaire combines deep research into technology infrastructure (undersea cables, satellite systems, internet governance) with study of African, South American, and indigenous healing and knowledge traditions (Kemetic yoga, plant medicine, ancestral technologies). She produces high-saturation digital video works that layer internet aesthetics (memes, screen recordings, browser windows) over spiritual and decolonial content. Increasingly, her practice has moved toward embodied healing work -- kundalini yoga, doula practice, and land-based projects at her space in French Guiana (Amakaba). She holds an MFA from Goldsmiths and studied at Wits School of Arts, Johannesburg.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Rezaire's practice directly challenges the extractive knowledge frameworks that A(DAI) seeks to avoid. Her work mapping colonial infrastructure embedded in digital networks provides essential critical perspective for any commons-first intelligence system. She brings Global South and indigenous epistemologies into technology discourse.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Partially. Her video works function as dense informational layers that could serve as conceptual substrate -- they encode complex networks of colonial history, technology infrastructure, and spiritual knowledge. Her healing practice and land-based work (Amakaba) function as living substrate for alternative knowledge production.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. Rezaire's work is fundamentally relational -- it maps connections between undersea cables and colonial trade routes, between internet governance and resource extraction, between ancestral knowledge and digital technology. The compositional logic is always about revealing hidden relationships between seemingly disparate systems.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially. Her video works are fixed, but her broader practice (Amakaba, healing work) is continuously evolving and responsive to community, land, and spiritual inputs. Her shift from digital art to embodied healing practice is itself a form of self-recomposition.

works.title: Deep Down Tidal
works.description: Video installation mapping the undersea fibre optic cable network and its overlap with colonial trade routes and slave shipping lanes. Reveals how digital infrastructure reproduces colonial geographic power structures.
works.relevance: Core example of decolonial technology critique -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s need to understand how infrastructure embeds power relations. Essential critical perspective for building commons-first systems.

works.title: Premium Connect
works.description: Video work exploring how internet infrastructure in Africa is controlled by former colonial powers and multinational corporations, connecting digital connectivity to resource extraction and data colonialism.
works.relevance: Exposes the extractive dynamics in technology infrastructure that A(DAI) aims to counter with commons-based alternatives.

works.title: Inner Fire
works.description: Immersive video installation exploring the science and spirituality of kundalini energy, connecting ancient healing knowledge to contemporary neuroscience and digital wellness culture.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how non-Western knowledge systems can be brought into technological discourse without reduction or extraction -- a methodology A(DAI) needs for genuinely inclusive intelligence.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Rezaire's work critiques existing protocols (internet governance, data infrastructure, colonial systems) rather than building new ones. Her practice exposes the hidden protocols embedded in technology and proposes ancestral/indigenous knowledge systems as alternative protocols for human-technology relations. Amakaba in French Guiana functions as a proto-protocol for land-based, decolonial knowledge production.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Amakaba: a residency and healing space in French Guiana that functions as alternative infrastructure for knowledge production outside Western institutional frameworks. Not a technical protocol but a social and spiritual one.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Rezaire's practice is deeply oriented toward challenging enclosure -- her work exposes how digital infrastructure encloses and extracts from Global South communities. Amakaba operates as commons-adjacent space for healing and knowledge sharing. However, her individual artworks circulate through the commercial gallery system (Goodman Gallery). She advocates for knowledge commons rooted in indigenous and ancestral traditions rather than Western open-source models.

governance_model.governance_detail: Solo artistic practice with community-oriented projects. Amakaba involves communal participation but is directed by Rezaire. Her gallery representation (Goodman Gallery, Johannesburg/London/New York) follows conventional artist-gallery model. Her healing practice operates through facilitator-participant structures.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Rezaire's decolonial framework implies deep attention to consent, particularly regarding the extraction and representation of indigenous and ancestral knowledge. Her healing practice requires participant consent. She is careful about how spiritual and indigenous knowledge is represented in art contexts, resisting extraction.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship for artworks. Her healing and teaching practice involves shared knowledge transmission. She explicitly positions her work as drawing from collective ancestral knowledge rather than claiming individual invention -- a model of authorship rooted in lineage rather than originality.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Individual video works are fixed once completed. However, her broader practice (Amakaba, healing work, teaching) is durational and continuously evolving. Her trajectory from digital art toward embodied healing represents a practice that transforms over time in response to personal and spiritual development.

data_materiality.data_sources: Research into internet infrastructure (submarine cable maps, satellite imagery, internet governance documents), colonial archives and trade route histories, indigenous and African healing traditions, kundalini yoga practice, neuroscience research, personal spiritual practice, land and ecology (French Guiana).
data_materiality.data_provenance: Research-based. Infrastructure data is drawn from public sources (submarine cable maps, governance documents). Indigenous and spiritual knowledge is accessed through personal study, lineage, and community engagement rather than extraction. Self-generated content through healing practice and embodied research.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Rezaire's work does not directly engage with ML embedding spaces. However, her practice operates in a conceptual 'embedding space' where colonial history, digital infrastructure, spiritual knowledge, and bodily experience are mapped onto shared coordinates -- revealing proximity and distance between seemingly unrelated domains.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. Spans video, installation, performance, healing/somatic practice, text, and land-based work.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Video installations typically presented as immersive environments with cushions, mats, and soft furnishings encouraging bodily relaxation -- blurring gallery and healing space. Exhibited at Serpentine Galleries, MoMA, Palais de Tokyo, Goodman Gallery, and international biennials. Amakaba operates as a non-gallery exhibition/residency space in French Guiana.

interoperability.composability: Limited in technical terms -- works are discrete art objects. Conceptually, her frameworks (decolonial infrastructure critique, ancestral technology) are highly composable as analytical lenses that can be applied across other works and systems.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed system in terms of technical outputs. Her ideas and frameworks circulate freely through lectures, publications, and interviews, but artworks are gallery-bound.

technical_approach.stack: Digital video production, screen capture and internet aesthetics, 3D animation and CGI, VR environments, multi-channel projection, sound design, custom installation environments (cushions, mats, lighting for immersive healing-adjacent spaces)

network_position.scene_affiliation: Decolonial technology art, Afrofuturism, Global South digital art, London/Goldsmiths network, Johannesburg art scene (Goodman Gallery, Wits), French Guiana/South American indigenous knowledge, international biennial circuit, healing and wellness practice, Serpentine Galleries, post-internet art
network_position.connections: Goodman Gallery (representation), Serpentine Galleries (exhibited), Palais de Tokyo (exhibited), MoMA (exhibited), Nora Khan (fellow decolonial technology thinker), American Artist (shared concerns re: race and technology), Sondra Perry (parallel practice), Legacy Russell (glitch feminism discourse). Bridges African, South American, and European art worlds; bridges digital art and healing/spiritual practice.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Rezaire's practice provides the essential decolonial critique that A(DAI) needs to avoid reproducing extractive knowledge frameworks. Her work mapping colonial infrastructure in digital networks is directly relevant to building genuinely commons-first systems. She could serve as a critical friend challenging A(DAI)'s assumptions about technology, knowledge, and openness from a Global South perspective. Her concept of ancestral knowledge as technology offers an alternative frame for what 'intelligence' means in collective intelligence.
